fact: The digital ministry's portal reports that a strategic seminar on 5-6 February 2026, under the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Ministry of Digital Affairs, marked a key step in drawing up Benin's digital strategy to 2031, with the drafting led by Deloitte.

The 5-6 February 2026 seminar brought public sector, private operators and technical partners together to define a vision, orientations and priority initiatives for the next five years of the 2031 digital strategy.

Benin launched consultations to draft a national digital strategy through 2031, formally starting the work at a Cotonou strategic workshop on 5-6 February 2026, covering internet coverage, e-services, artificial intelligence, digital skills and financing.

La Nation reported on 6 February 2026 that a two-day strategic workshop in Cotonou, with Deloitte providing technical support, aimed at drawing up Benin's digital strategy to 2031, to set the vision and priority initiatives for the next five years.

The GSMA study says the government has set out a digital strategy for the next three years, in line with the Government Action Programme 2021-2026; no adopting act is named, and the document is dated January 2025 (the supporting budget presentation is November 2023).

The study says the digital strategy is overseen by the Ministry of Digital Economy and implemented through ARCEP and the Agency for Information Systems and Digital Technology (ASIN); it gives no date, so its published date of January 2025 applies.

The Minister for Digitalisation's budget presentation to the National Assembly's budget committee in November 2023 said CFA 12.79 billion would be used for digital transformation projects, which the study lists among the strategy's priorities.

The study says the World Bank support programme of the Government Action Programme and the digital strategy, with digitalisation of public service delivery as a key priority, is a USD 150 million funded programme with targets to December 2028 (World Bank report of August 2024).
